root_cause.text: dm-cache enforced the “passthrough mode requires all cache blocks to be clean” check too early in `cache_create()` instead of at resume time, so with table preloading the inactive cache table could be switched to passthrough while dirty mappings were still being loaded from shared metadata in `load_mapping()`, allowing dirty data to enter passthrough mode.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `dm_cache_metadata_all_clean()` check from `cache_create()` and instead adds a dirty-mapping rejection in `load_mapping()` when `passthrough_mode(cache)` is active, plus it updates `cache_preresume()` to tolerate `-EBUSY`; the CVE description explicitly says the check was “performed during table creation” and “fails with preload while metadata updates are ongoing,” which “risks loading dirty mappings into passthrough mode, resulting in data loss.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused `dm_cache_metadata_all_clean` helper from the cache metadata code.
intent_record.what: The function `dm_cache_metadata_all_clean(struct dm_cache_metadata *cmd, bool *result)` was removed entirely, including its local variable, read lock/unlock, and call to `blocks_are_unmapped_or_clean(cmd, 0, cmd->cache_blocks, result)`.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the `dm_cache_metadata_all_clean` entry point, so callers can no longer query whether all cache metadata blocks are unmapped or clean through this function. Runtime behavior for the remaining code is unaffected in this hunk, but any external references to this function would fail to compile or link until updated or removed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the obsolete all-clean metadata query from the public cache metadata API.
intent_record.what: The declaration of `dm_cache_metadata_all_clean(struct dm_cache_metadata *cmd, bool *result);` and its associated comment were removed from the header, leaving the surrounding metadata API declarations unchanged.
intent_record.how: This removes the public interface for querying whether all cache blocks are clean, so code outside this unit can no longer call that metadata check through this header.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allow passthrough mode cache creation to proceed without requiring an all-clean metadata check, while still disabling migrations.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the block inside cache_create() that, when passthrough_mode(cache) is true, called dm_cache_metadata_all_clean(), checked the all_clean result, and returned an error if metadata was not clean. The remaining code now only calls policy_allow_migrations(cache->policy, false) under the passthrough_mode(cache) condition.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cache creation in passthrough mode no longer verifies that all cached blocks are clean before proceeding. As a result, the function will no longer fail with -EINVAL or a metadata-read error from dm_cache_metadata_all_clean() at this point, and it will simply disable migrations when passthrough mode is enabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject dirty mappings during passthrough mode to prevent entering passthrough with non-clean cache blocks.
intent_record.what: Inside load_mapping(), a new conditional was added at the start of the dirty-block path: if passthrough_mode(cache) is true, it logs an error with DMERR and returns -EBUSY before setting the dirty bit or incrementing nr_dirty.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the mapping loader from marking blocks dirty while the cache is in passthrough mode, causing the operation to fail instead of allowing a state transition that requires all blocks to be clean.

intent_record.intent_summary: Treat `-EBUSY` like `-EFBIG` during cache mapping load failures by not reporting it as a metadata operation failure.
intent_record.what: In cache_preresume(), the error check after load_filtered_mapping() was changed from `if (r != -EFBIG)` to `if (r != -EFBIG && r != -EBUSY)` before calling metadata_operation_failed().
intent_record.how: This change prevents `metadata_operation_failed()` from being invoked when `load_filtered_mapping()` fails with `-EBUSY`, while preserving the existing special-case handling for `-EFBIG`. Runtime behavior still returns the original error, but one additional failure mode is no longer treated as a metadata operation failure.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the obsolete all-clean metadata query from the public cache metadata API.
Allow passthrough mode cache creation to proceed without requiring an all-clean metadata check, while still disabling migrations.
Reject dirty mappings during passthrough mode to prevent entering passthrough with non-clean cache blocks.
Treat `-EBUSY` like `-EFBIG` during cache mapping load failures by not reporting it as a metadata operation failure.

consistency_review.core_intent: Remove the obsolete all-clean metadata query/helper from the cache metadata code and public API.

relevance_review.reason: The changes only remove an obsolete metadata helper/API for checking whether cache blocks are all clean. They do not alter the passthrough-mode timing in cache_create() versus resume time, nor do they address dirty mappings being loaded during table preloading.

The change directly matches the root cause: it alters passthrough mode handling by removing the all-clean check during cache creation, which is the same early-enforcement issue that allowed dirty mappings to be loaded before passthrough mode was safely applied.

The change directly matches the vulnerability’s core issue: it prevents dirty mappings from being accepted while in passthrough mode, addressing the unsafe transition where dirty cache blocks could exist during passthrough.

The change only adjusts error handling for mapping load failures (-EBUSY vs -EFBIG) and does not address the passthrough-mode cleanliness check timing or the race between cache creation, table preloading, and dirty mapping loading described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This is the guard that triggers the too-early passthrough validation during cache_create(), which is the direct root cause: the check runs before table preloading/load_mapping() has finished loading shared metadata, so dirty mappings can still be introduced afterward.

This call performs the all-clean metadata check at the wrong time. The vulnerability stems from enforcing cleanliness during creation instead of resume, allowing later-loaded dirty mappings to bypass the intended constraint.

This conditional embodies the incorrect early rejection logic for passthrough mode. Because it is evaluated before preloaded mappings are fully loaded, it can incorrectly authorize passthrough before dirty mappings appear.

Disabling migrations is part of passthrough handling, but doing so here after an early clean check contributes to the flawed creation-time state transition that lets dirty data enter passthrough mode later during loading.

This line records dirty mappings into cache metadata. In the vulnerable flow, dirty mappings can be loaded after the premature passthrough check, so this is the mechanism by which dirty data enters passthrough mode.

vuln_statements.explanation: This branch enters the premature passthrough-mode validation during cache creation. The root cause is that the clean-cache requirement is enforced too early in cache_create(), before table preloading/load_mapping() finishes loading shared metadata.

This is the actual all-clean check being performed at the wrong time. It should not run during creation because dirty mappings may still be loaded afterward, allowing passthrough mode to be entered with dirty blocks.

This conditional enforces the incorrect early rejection/acceptance logic for passthrough mode. Because it is evaluated before preload completes, it can incorrectly validate passthrough even though dirty mappings may appear later.

This disables migrations as part of passthrough handling, but in the vulnerable flow it is tied to the too-early creation-time transition. That leaves the cache in passthrough mode while dirty mappings can still be introduced during loading.
